review.summary: Adjudication of the four network/design reviews (R5-R8) and independent audits (`audit/LATTICE_LINE_AUDIT.json`, `audit/GRAPH_COUNTEREXAMPLES.json`, `audit/SOURCE_CHECK_NOTES.md`) confirms that the current sweep (`network/oxt/materials.py`, `network/oxt/network.py`, `network/run_sweep.py`) confounds topological connectivity with constitutive stiffening and batch-coupled relaxation, while several reviewer assertions require mathematical correction. Specifically: (1) On the staggered periodic triangular lattice, the line-tracing loop produces `2W` cycles (`W` horizontal of length `W`, and `W/2` in each diagonal direction of length `2W`), so one forced cut per cycle leaves expected coordination `E[z] = 6p(1 - 2/(3W))` rather than `6p(1 - 1/W)` (`E[z] = 3.4756` at `W=16` and `3.4180` at `W=64` for `z_target=3.4`). However, R5's claim that mean fiber length scales linearly with `W` is false because independent bond dilution (`1 - p ~ 0.35-0.43`) truncates contiguous segments to `O(1/(1-p))` lattice units regardless of `W`. (2) R5's claim that affine GAG tethers (`k_gag > 0`) guarantee `G > 0` at zero collagen connectivity and `mu_el = 0` is algebraically false: with zero bonds, `E = 0.5 * k_gag * sum |x_i - F X_i|^2` is minimized to `0` for all `F` by `x_i = F X_i`, giving `G = 0`. Nonzero `mu_el` provides a true full-lattice elastic floor, while `k_gag` penalizes non-affine relaxation of connected fragments. (3) Oxidative `dose` simultaneously adds `n_bridge` edges, re-closes cut periodic lines, activates collinear bending on bridges, double-embrittles bridges sampled again in `present` (`brittle^2`), and locks node angles using a single unweighted `k_rel`, while clamping anisotropic bridge counts when `z_target >= 4.92`. (4) Connectivity, clustering, and hub bias have strict identifiability limits on a fixed `k <= 6` lattice: `mesh_size` (`E - V`) is blind to components and degree-preserving rewiring; exact counterexamples show identical degree sequences and clustering yield different giant components; growing Barabasi-Albert power laws are impossible; and hexagon plaquette flips preserve degrees and directional bond counts but still alter collinear bending pairs `N_bend`. (5) Reusing base seeds across treatments is valid common-random-number variance reduction if streams are separated by mechanism, whereas sequential single-stream consumption in `build_spec` and pre-cell `groupby.mean()` averaging break statistical control. Generic central-force pebble games, L-BFGS iteration counts as physical relaxation times, and universal `z_c`/`ftol`/`80%` cutoffs are rejected in favor of Hessian-validated, per-system converged, held-out active learning. This output is a static review and experimental design specification, not an executed simulation or a live AlphaEvolve service.

findings.title: Periodic line-cycle algebra (`2W` vs `3W` lines) shifts expected coordination `z`, whereas R5's claim that mean fiber length scales linearly with `W` is false
findings.evidence: In `network/oxt/materials.py` (lines 88-92), `build_spec` computes `p = min(1.0, z / 6.0 / (1 - 1.0 / lat.W))` assuming `3W` cycles of length `W`. However, the staggered periodic neighbor map in `network/oxt/network.py` (lines 49-51, 88-100) generates `W` horizontal cycles of length `W` and `W/2` cycles of length `2W` in each diagonal direction (`n_lines = 2W`, verified in `audit/LATTICE_LINE_AUDIT.json` lines 4-71). In `audit/NETWORK_REVIEWS.json` (lines 27-33), R5 further claimed that cutting one bond per line forces mean fiber length to scale linearly with `W`.
findings.implication: Cutting one bond per cycle removes `2W` candidate sites out of `Nb = 3W^2`, yielding pre-bridging expected coordination `E[z_realized] = 6p(1 - 2/(3W)) = z_target * (1 - 2/(3W)) / (1 - 1/W)` (`3.5619` at `W=8`, `3.4756` at `W=16`, `3.4180` at `W=64` for `z_target = 3.4`), introducing a `W`-dependent density drift if plotted against `z_target`. Conversely, R5's claim that mean fiber length grows linearly with `W` is mathematically incorrect: although the forced cut bounds the maximum cycle length at `W - 1` (horizontal) and `2W - 1` (diagonal), independent Bernoulli dilution breaks bonds at rate `1 - p` (`~0.35-0.43`), so mean contiguous fiber contour length converges to `O(1/(1-p))` (~2.5 segments) independent of `W` when `p < 1`.
findings.recommended_check: Correct the dilution normalization in `network/oxt/materials.py` line 88 to `p = min(1.0, z / 6.0 / (1.0 - 2.0 / (3.0 * lat.W)))`, analyze existing sweeps strictly against the recorded realized `z` (`network/run_sweep.py` line 69) rather than relabeling `z_target`, and directly log the empirical distribution of contiguous collinear fiber lengths `L_f` across `W in {16, 32, 64}` to verify when `E[L_f]` is governed by `1/(1-p)` versus finite-`W` line cuts at `p -> 1`.

findings.title: Adjudication of background springs (`k_gag` zero-bond counterexample vs `mu_el`), batch-summed L-BFGS coupling, and invalid generic rigidity shortcuts
findings.evidence: In `network/oxt/network.py`, `Batch.energy` includes background elastin `mu_eff = self.mu * a + self.mu_el` on all `3N` bonds (line 155) and affine node tethers `0.5 * k_gag * (x - xa)^2` where `xa = X @ F^T` (lines 172-173), while `Batch.relax` minimizes `e.sum()` across the batch and stops when batch-wide `fmax < ftol * 10` and `abs(e_prev - e_now) <= 1e-10 * abs(e_now) + 1e-18` (lines 174, 198-200). In `audit/NETWORK_REVIEWS.json`, R5 claimed `k_gag > 0` alone guarantees `G > 0` at `z = 0` (line 11) and proposed standard 2-core/pebble-game rigidity metrics (line 52), while R7 used L-BFGS iteration count as a relaxation-regime observable (line 205).
findings.implication: R5's zero-connectivity claim is false: when `alive = 0` and `mu_el = 0`, all bond/angle terms vanish and `0.5 * k_gag * sum |x_i - F X_i|^2` attains its exact minimum `0` at the affine state `x_i = F X_i` for every `F`, yielding `dE/dF = 0` and `G = 0` (`audit/SOURCE_CHECK_NOTES.md` line 30). Instead, `mu_el > 0` creates a true `z = 6` elastic floor, whereas `k_gag > 0` suppresses non-affine relaxation (`x_i != F X_i`) of connected collagen clusters. R5, R7, and R8 correctly identify that summing `e.sum()` in `Batch.relax` lets stiff systems dominate `abs(e_now)` and line searches, halting floppy systems prematurely. However, generic central-force `(2,3)` pebble games or `k`-cores do not certify rigidity when 3-body bending (`kappa`), 6-spoke angular locks (`kx`), prestrain, and tethers are present, and L-BFGS iteration counts reflect quasi-Newton conditioning rather than physical viscoelastic relaxation time.
findings.recommended_check: Enforce per-system stopping criteria in `Batch.relax` using `per_system=True` energies and per-system gradient norms, verify step-size invariance (`eps in {1e-4, 2e-3}`) rather than imposing an unachievable universal `ftol`, run ablations with `mu_el = 0` and `k_gag in {0, 1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4}`, and replace generic pebble-game/iteration-count proxies with exact dynamical-matrix (Hessian) rank, zero-mode fraction, and Schur-complement linear shear modulus `G_0`.

findings.title: Oxidative `dose` confounds five structural/constitutive changes, double-embrittles bridge bonds (`brittle^2`), and clamps anisotropic bridges at high `z`
findings.evidence: In `build_spec` (`network/oxt/materials.py` lines 101-138), `dmg.dose > 0` averages `k_rel` across chemistries (line 102), activates `n_bridge` missing bonds (`alive[new] = True`, line 116) with `eps_r[new] = col.eps_r * dmg.brittle` (line 118) while leaving `kb[new] = 1.0` (line 95), defines `present = np.flatnonzero(alive)` after adding `new` (line 121) and multiplies `eps_r[chosen] *= dmg.brittle` again (line 133), and locks `n_lock` random junctions across all `lat.N` nodes (line 137). In `aniso` mode, bridges are drawn only from `missing[on_axis[missing]]` (line 114).
findings.implication: Dose sweeps cannot distinguish topological percolation from constitutive stiffening because increasing `dose` simultaneously: (1) increases coordination `z` by up to `+0.36`, (2) reconnects forced periodic line cuts from line 92, (3) creates collinear bending fibers across bridge bonds (`network/oxt/network.py` lines 162-163), (4) subjects newly added bridges to a compounded `dmg.brittle^2` (`0.2025x`) rupture strain reduction whenever re-selected in `chosen`, and (5) adds angular springs even on degree-0/1 nodes. Furthermore, because a single lattice axis has only `N = Nb/3` bonds, `missing[on_axis[missing]]` has fewer than `n_bridge = 0.18 N` missing bonds whenever `p > 0.82` (`z_target >= 4.92`, affecting `z = 5.0, 5.4` in `network/run_sweep.py` lines 34, 39), silently clamping `aniso` edge additions below `iso`.
findings.recommended_check: Sample `present = np.flatnonzero(alive)` prior to setting `alive[new] = True` (or explicitly test single- vs double-hit embrittlement as an ablation), add a boolean mask or `kb[new] = 0` option so inter-fiber bridges do not form continuous collinear bending segments or re-close periodic lines, restrict `rigid_node` to nodes with alive degree `>= 2`, log directional edge counts `(E_0, E_1, E_2)` to flag `aniso` saturation, and decouple `k_rel` into separate stretch, bending, and angular stiffness multipliers.

findings.title: Identifiability limits of connectivity, clustering, and hub bias on a bounded (`k <= 6`) triangular lattice and blindness of Euler `mesh_size`
findings.evidence: `Lattice.__init__` (`network/oxt/network.py` lines 51-73) restricts candidate edges to `3N` unit bonds with maximum node degree `k_max = 6` and collinear bending pairs `(bend_in, bend_out)`. `mesh_size` (lines 295-302) computes `faces = max(E - V, 1)` from total alive edges `E` and non-isolated vertices `V`. Meanwhile, `audit/GRAPH_COUNTEREXAMPLES.json` (lines 3-219) exhibits three 2-regular 12-node graphs (one 12-cycle, two 6-cycles, four 3-cycles) with identical degree sequences.
findings.implication: First, `mesh_size` omits the connected component count `C` (`faces = E - V + C` for planar graphs) and is algebraically invariant to any degree-preserving rewiring at fixed `E` and `V`. Second, as `audit/GRAPH_COUNTEREXAMPLES.json` proves, mean degree `z`, exact degree sequence `{k_i}`, and clustering `C` do not uniquely determine giant-component connectivity (`S_1/N` is `1.0` vs `0.5` at `C = 0`, and `0.25` at `C = 1`). Third, on the fixed `k <= 6` lattice, growing Barabasi-Albert preferential attachment and power-law tails are impossible (`evidence/PRIMARY_SOURCES.md` lines 13-15); only bounded degree variance `Var(k)` on fixed nodes can be tested. Fourth, every triangle uses one bond from each direction (`T <= 2 min(E_0, E_1, E_2)`), coupling clustering to anisotropy, and even degree- and direction-preserving elementary hexagon plaquette flips alter active collinear bending pairs `N_bend` (`audit/SOURCE_CHECK_NOTES.md` line 41).
findings.recommended_check: Replace `mesh_size` reliance with exact topological metrics: periodic torus-wrapping probabilities `R_wrap`, largest-component fraction `S_1/N`, finite-cluster susceptibility `chi`, triangle count `T`, degree variance `Var(k)`, assortativity `r_deg`, and active collinear pair count `N_bend`. When testing clustering via hexagon plaquette flips or fixed-node hub bias via constrained swaps, explicitly record the feasible `(T, Var(k), N_bend)` range, autocorrelation mixing times `tau_int`, and condition mechanical comparisons on matched `(E_0, E_1, E_2, N_bend)`.

findings.title: Sequential RNG stream coupling in `build_spec`, pre-cell replicate averaging (`groupby.mean`), and unvalidated reviewer threshold shortcuts
findings.evidence: `_worker` (`network/run_sweep.py` line 60) initializes a single `rng = np.random.default_rng(it['seed'])` passed to `build_spec`, where it is drawn sequentially for dilution (line 89), line cuts (line 92), bridging (line 109), stiffening (line 128), and node locking (line 137); `stage_network` reuses `seed = 1000 + s` across grid points (lines 133, 136), and `stage_cell`/`stage_organ` average across seeds via `groupby(...).mean()` (lines 160-162, 190) before evaluating nonlinear cell bistability and tearing (lines 180-182).
findings.implication: Contrary to R7 (`audit/NETWORK_REVIEWS.json` lines 157-160), reusing a base graph seed across treatments is valid common-random-number pairing when analysis blocks on graph identity (`audit/SOURCE_CHECK_NOTES.md` line 39). The actual design flaw is that a single RNG stream is shared across mechanisms inside `build_spec`, so changing `n_bridge` shifts the random numbers used for `stiff_frac` and `rigid_frac`, breaking paired counterfactuals. Furthermore, collapsing replicates with `groupby.mean()` before passing secant curves to the nonlinear `CellModel` erases replicate variance and biases bistability/tearing classifications via Jensen's inequality. Finally, reviewer falsifiers relying on arbitrary cutoffs (`>= 80%` stiffness share, `> 1%` mean force, `Delta_AIC < 2`, or interpreting a 95% CI containing zero as proof of no effect) are statistically invalid without a pre-specified minimum scientifically meaningful effect size (SESOI) and smooth-null held-out testing.
findings.recommended_check: Split RNG streams per mechanism via `SeedSequence((base_seed, mechanism_id))` so base graph dilution, line cuts, bridging, stiffening, and angle locking use orthogonal draws; propagate individual graph replicates through `stage_cell` and `stage_organ` before computing hierarchical/paired bootstrap confidence intervals; and evaluate regime transitions against a smooth monotone null model on held-out seeds and lattice sizes using pre-specified equivalence bounds.

review.strongest_surviving_claim: Within the implemented 2D periodic diluted triangular lattice (`network/oxt/network.py` and `network/oxt/materials.py`), the energy formulation for bond stretching, collinear 3-body bending, 6-spoke junction angle locking, background elastin, and affine GAG tethers is mathematically well-defined and differentiable; across fixed finite lattices (`W = 16`, 4 seeds), increasing realized coordination `z` or applying the composite oxidative damage protocol monotonically increases small-strain shear modulus `G`, reduces the secant stiffening ratio `sigma(gamma)/(gamma * G)`, and produces directional stiffness anisotropy (`Cx/Cy > 1`) when edge additions and bond stiffening are preferentially aligned with one lattice axis.
review.decisive_next_experiment:
Distinction of scope: This document is a completed static adversarial review and experimental design specification; no code or simulation has been executed here, and deploying a closed-loop simulator or an evolutionary code-search service (such as AlphaEvolve) requires a separately scoped execution workflow with deterministic evaluators and locked held-out tests.

Practical Staged Experimental Matrix (recommendations for next simulation campaign):

1. STAGE 0 (Code & RNG Deconfounding Prerequisites):
   - Fix dilution normalization in `network/oxt/materials.py` line 88 to `p = min(1.0, z / 6.0 / (1.0 - 2.0 / (3.0 * lat.W)))` so expected pre-bridging coordination matches `z_target` across `W`, while always analyzing against realized `z`.
   - Split RNG streams via `np.random.SeedSequence((rep_seed, stream_id))` into 5 orthogonal streams (base dilution, line cuts, bridge addition, segment stiffening, node locking) to enable exact common-random-number paired comparisons across interventions on identical base graphs.
   - Sample `present = np.flatnonzero(alive)` before `alive[new] = True` (with an explicit toggle to ablate single-hit `brittle` vs compounded `brittle^2` on bridges), restrict `rigid_node` to nodes with alive degree `>= 2`, and enforce per-system convergence in `Batch.relax` (`per_system=True`, per-system `fmax_i < 1e-7`, per-system relative energy change `< 1e-11`, verified for step-size invariance at `eps in {1e-4, 2e-3}`).

2. STAGE 1 (Factorial Mechanism & Background Ablation at `W in {16, 32}`):
   - Priority 1A (Background & Constraint Tiers at `dose = 0`): Sweep realized `z in [2.0, 5.4]` (16 independent Newman-Ziff bond-insertion permutations per `W`, treating each permutation as one correlated curve replicate, never treating nested snapshots as independent points) across four physics tiers: (T1) pure central-force (`kappa = 0, kx = 0, mu_el = 0, k_gag = 0`), (T2) central-force + collinear bending (`kappa = 3e-3, kx = 0, mu_el = 0, k_gag = 0`), (T3) central-force + bending + junction locks (`kx = 2e-3, mu_el = 0, k_gag = 0`), and (T4) background sensitivity (`mu_el in {0, 0.005}`, `k_gag in {0, 1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4}`).
   - Priority 1B (Orthogonal Damage Decomposition at matched base seeds and matched realized `z`): At sub-isostatic (`z_0 = 3.0`), near-crossover (`z_0 = 3.6`), and super-isostatic (`z_0 = 4.4`) baselines, compare: (D0) baseline dilution matched to post-bridge `z_actual = z_0 + delta_z`; (D1a) topological bridging with `kb[new] = 0` and native `(mu, eps_r)` preserving one cut per periodic line; (D1b) bridging allowing periodic line re-closure and collinear bending (`kb[new] = 1`); (D2) pure intrafibrillar stiffening/embrittlement at fixed `alive` (`bridge_frac = 0, rigid_frac = 0`, separating `mu/kb` stiffening from `brittle`); and (D3) pure junction angle locking at fixed `alive` (`bridge_frac = 0, stiff_frac = 0`).

3. STAGE 2 (Constrained Spatial Topology Ensembles — Quantifying Connectivity, Clustering, and Hub Bias at `W in {16, 32}`):
   - Hold node count `N = W^2`, bond count `E = zN/2`, unit bond length, and constitutive parameters fixed (`mu_el = 0, k_gag = 0` vs `k_gag = 1e-6`).
   - (E1 — Pure Triangle Clustering via Elementary Hexagon Plaquette Flips): Apply alternating 6-cycle flips on the triangular lattice, which strictly preserve every node's exact degree `{k_i}` (hence `Var(k)`) and directional bond counts `(E_0, E_1, E_2)`, using a Metropolis target `exp(beta_T * T - beta_b * (N_bend - N_bend,0)^2)` to vary triangle transitivity across its feasible polytope `[T_min, T_max]` while holding collinear bending pairs `N_bend` matched within `+/- 1%` (and running an unconstrained-`N_bend` control to measure the bending-clustering coupling).
   - (E2 — Fixed-Node Bounded Hub Bias): Apply canonical lattice edge swaps targeting `exp(beta_k * sum_i k_i^2 - beta_T * (T - T_0)^2 - beta_b * (N_bend - N_bend,0)^2)` to vary bounded degree variance `Var(k)` (`0 <= k_i <= 6`) at matched `(z, T, N_bend)`.
   - Feasibility & Mixing Controls: Record MCMC acceptance rates and integrated autocorrelation times `tau_int`; require burn-in and thinning `>= 50 * tau_int` swaps per independent chain; flag parameter combinations where the feasible polytope width `T_max - T_min` vanishes (e.g., strong directional anisotropy).

4. STAGE 3 (Expected-Information-Gain Controller & Independent Held-Out Validation at `W = 64`):
   - Vaulted Held-Out Split: Before any adaptive sampling, lock in a read-only vault: (i) 25% of space-filling Latin-hypercube parameter points at `W in {16, 32}`, (ii) 16 independent graph seeds per condition, and (iii) all out-of-sample finite-size scaling runs at `W = 64` (16 seeds per point).
   - Expected-Information-Gain (EIG) Controller: Fit a heteroscedastic Gaussian Process / bootstrap ensemble surrogate to Stage 1-2 exploration data; select sequential batches `x` by maximizing compute-normalized EIG regarding competing regime models `M_m` (smooth monotone spline null vs piecewise/crossover scaling model) and partial derivatives `(d ln G / dT, d ln G / d Var(k))`: `Acquisition(x, W) = I(y; M, theta | x, W, D_train) / E[t_wall(x, W)]`, blended with `25%` quasi-random Sobol exploration so classifier/boundary evaluation is never performed on adaptively cherry-picked points.
   - Recorded Observables: Realized `z`, `(E_0, E_1, E_2)`, giant component `S_1/N`, torus wrapping `R_wrap(x, y)`, susceptibility `chi`, triangle count `T`, global transitivity, `Var(k)`, `r_deg`, active bending pairs `N_bend`, empirical fiber length distribution `L_f`, exact Hessian rank / zero-mode fraction `f_0` / Schur-complement linear shear modulus `G_0`, per-system L-BFGS `G(eps)`, central-difference tangent modulus `G_tan(gamma) = dP_xy/dgamma`, non-affinity `Gamma(gamma)`, forward-reverse shear hysteresis loop area, peak stress, strain at peak, toughness, and replicate-level cell `YAP_NC` and `bistable` indicators (without pre-averaging).
   - Convergence & Stopping Criteria: Stop adaptive acquisition when the 95% bootstrap CI width on the operational crossover interval `[z_10(W), z_50(W)]` is `<= 0.05` in `z`, or when held-out log-predictive density difference `Delta_ELPD` between competing models changes by `< 5%` over two consecutive rounds.
   - Falsifier & Equivalence Criterion: Pre-specify the smallest scientifically meaningful effect size (SESOI) as `|Delta ln G| >= 0.10` (`~10%` modulus change across the feasible interquartile range of `T` or `Var(k)` at fixed `z, E_0, E_1, E_2, N_bend`). (i) If on the vaulted held-out set (`W = 64`), matching realized `z_actual` and preventing periodic line re-closure (`D1a` vs `D0`) reduces the incremental `dose` effect on `ln G` within the equivalence bound `[-0.10, +0.10]` while `D2 + D3` (stiffening + angle locking at fixed graph `alive`) accounts for the remaining shift, the hypothesis that oxidative damage stiffens networks via topological connectivity percolation is falsified. (ii) If across `W in {32, 64}` the held-out `Delta_ELPD` of a critical/piecewise scaling model over a smooth monotone spline null is `<= 0` (or `R_wrap` and `G_0/G_affine` curves fail to sharpen with `W`), reject claims of a sharp thermodynamic rigidity transition and report only an operational finite-size crossover interval. (iii) If the 95% CI for `Delta ln G` across feasible `T` (E1) or `Var(k)` (E2) at matched `(z, E_0, E_1, E_2, N_bend)` lies entirely within `[-0.10, +0.10]`, independent clustering or fixed-node hub-variance effects are falsified in favor of coordination and bending-pair count; if the 95% CI overlaps both `0` and `+/- 0.10`, report the topological effect as statistically unresolved rather than absent.
